name: GitLab
description: GitLab Community Edition: Git hosting with merge requests, issues, CI/CD, a container and package registry and a wiki, all in the one Omnibus image. It is heavy — at least 4 GB of memory and several minutes for the first start — and the CI runners that execute pipelines are registered separately.

access.note: GitLab creates its administrator on the first start: sign in as root with the generated GITLAB_ROOT_PASSWORD from the Variables tab. It is read only on that first start, so change the password inside GitLab afterwards, and turn off open sign-up under Admin → Settings → General if you do not want it. Git over SSH listens on port 22 inside the container and is not published; clone over HTTPS.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: GitLab's external URL: clone URLs, links and the registry are built from it.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The web interface, the API and Git over HTTPS

volumes.name: config
volumes.purpose: gitlab.rb and the secrets GitLab generates

volumes.name: data
volumes.purpose: Repositories, the bundled PostgreSQL and Redis, uploads and artifacts

startup.name: GITLAB_OMNIBUS_CONFIG
startup.value: external_url 'https://{{input.domain}}'; nginx['listen_port'] = 80; nginx['listen_https'] = false; letsencrypt['enable'] = false; prometheus_monitoring['enable'] = false; puma['worker_processes'] = 2; sidekiq['concurrency'] = 10

update.notes: GitLab must be upgraded along its documented upgrade path, one required stop at a time; take a backup with gitlab-backup and keep /etc/gitlab/gitlab-secrets.json beside it.

secrets.name: root-password
secrets.label: Administrator password
secrets.description: The first password of the root account.
